newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish Handlowy bank sell-off on track - official.
newsitem.headline: Polish Handlowy bank sell-off on track - official.

text.p: The privatisation of Poland's largest commercial bank, Bank Handlowy SA, is on track and the government is likely to give a final go ahead for the sale on Tuesday, a senior government official said.
The official, who asked not to be named, confirmed that by the end of June the government would offer to the public 30 percent of Handlowy's shares.
Before the flotation, a 30-percent stake would be sold to a group of institutional investors as earlier planned, the official said.
"On Tuesday, the government should give its approval for selling the Handlowy shares...," the official told Reuters.

Under the government plan, another 30 percent will be set aside to strengthen assets of pension funds to be created under Poland's reform of the social security system. The remainder will go the bank's employees and the treasury.

The official said that by the end of the week British investment bank Schroders was likely to sign an agreement with the treasury ministry on advising it on the Handlowy sale. Schroeders is already advising Handlowy on the privatisation. @
The ministry would soon additionally select an advising firm, which would help it determine Handlowy's value.

According to preliminary results, Handlowy netted 555 million zlotys in 1996 up from 425 million in 1995. At the end of 1996 the bank had a balance sheet total of 13.31 billion zlotys, up 51.3 percent from 1995.
